# Load packages

```{r load-packages, eval = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
```

# Exercises

## Exercise 1 — Glimpse and describe (5 points)

**Goal:** Inspect the size and variable types of `penguins`.

```{r glimpse-penguins, eval = FALSE}
glimpse(penguins)
```

> There are 344 rows and 8 variables. There are 3 categorical variables and 5 numerical variables.

## Exercise 2 — Variable names (5 points)

**Goal:** Explain why the column names are “good.”

```{r names-penguins, eval = FALSE}
names(penguins)
```

> The column names are good names in R syntax because it is in snake case, which means its all in lowercase and any spaces use underscore.

## Exercise 3 — Count by species (5 points)

**Goal:** Produce a frequency table.

```{r count-species, eval = FALSE}
penguins %>%
count(species)
```

> You can also use group_by() and summarize().

## Exercise 4 — Bar plot by island and species (5 points)

**Goal:** Visualize counts by island, filled by species, and report where each species was observed.

```{r visualize-penguin-island-species, eval = FALSE}
penguins %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_classic()
```

> The species were observed at Biscoe, Dream, and Togersen.

## Exercise 5 — Scatter plot of body mass and flipper length (5 points)

**Goal:** Visualize the relationship and note a species difference.

```{r visualize-penguin-body-mass, eval = FALSE}
penguins %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, color = species, shape = species)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_classic()
```

> There seems to be a positive correlation between the two variables. The Gentoo penguins have generally higher flipper lengths and body masses than the other species.
